turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you recommend a good board game for just two players?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Jaipur is a great one. It's a quick trading game, about twenty minutes, and easy to learn.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We like something / a bit more strategic, actually.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then try Seven Wonders Duel. It's still under an hour, but there's lots to plan.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is that one hard to learn?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The first game takes a bit of rule checking, but after that it flows nicely. Most couples play it again right away.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sounds perfect. We'll get that one.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Enjoy! Fair warning, it gets pretty competitive.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My friends always argue about the rules in Monopoly. How do we stop that?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Agree on house rules before you start, like what happens on free parking. Writing them on a note helps.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The game also takes forever.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The official rules include auctions when someone skips a property. Using them makes the game much faster.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I had no idea. What else?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You can set a time limit, like ninety minutes, and whoever has the most money then wins.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, maybe / we should just play a different game.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's an option too. Catan has a similar trading feel and usually ends in about an hour.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My game box is a disaster. All the cards and tokens are mixed together.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Small zip bags are the cheapest fix. One bag per type of piece, and setup gets much quicker.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Some people buy / those fancy wooden inserts, right?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, they're nice for games you play a lot. For everything else, bags or little plastic boxes do the job.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about cards getting worn out?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Card sleeves protect them. They're worth it for games where you shuffle a lot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'll start with the bags this weekend.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good plan. Label each bag and your future self will thank you.

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's fine, it uses pictures only. Another favorite is Hoot Owl Hoot, which is all colors.

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's still great for counting practice. It's pure luck though, so mix it with one where they make choices.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll get the owl one then.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lovely. Games for that age usually last about fifteen minutes, just right for little attention spans.

option_sets.lead_in: We're having game night on Friday, and I need to pick what to buy.
options: The first one is a big strategy game about building cities, about two hours to play.
Then there's a quick party game with drawing and guessing that works for up to ten people.
Option three is a cooperative game where everyone works together to stop a spreading disease.
And the last one is a word game with cards that's short and pretty easy to learn.
moshi_comment: If lots of people are coming, the drawing party game is the safest choice, it's easy and loud and fun. The strategy game is great for a small, serious group. The cooperative game is nice if some people don't enjoy competing.
How many people are coming, and are they into games? For a big casual crowd, the party game wins. For four keen players, I'd go with the city building one.

option_sets.lead_in: I want a board game to play with my partner on quiet evenings.
options: One is a two player card game about trading spices, fast and really easy to set up.
Another is a puzzle style game where you build a pretty garden with tiles.
Or there's a long campaign game where the story changes every time you play.
moshi_comment: The spice trading game is perfect for quick evenings, you can play a few rounds after dinner. The garden tile game is relaxing and looks lovely on the table. The campaign game is the most immersive but needs a real time commitment.
Do you two like to compete, or would you rather relax? For relaxing, the garden game is a lovely pick. If you want something to look forward to each week, try the campaign game.
